newsitem.title: USA: CFTC's Born opposes futures "pro-market" exemption.
newsitem.headline: CFTC's Born opposes futures "pro-market" exemption.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission chairman Brooksley Born reiterated her opposition to deregulating U.S. futures markets and said she strongly opposed the so-called pro-market exemption.

Speaking to an annual futures industry conference here, Born said that while a review of the Commodity Exchange Act was appropriate, she thought current legislation to streamline the act was dangerous.
"The Commission strongly opposes the professional market exemption in the pending bills, which would lead to pervasive deregulation of our futures exchanges," Born said.
Born said the Futures Industry Association, the host of the conference, was taking a position "diametrically oppposed" to the CFTC's.

"It does surprise me that the FIA -- whose members depend so heavily on the integrity of the futures markets and investor confidence in them -- has supported the removal of the regulatory protections that have made our markets the safest and most transparent in the world," she said.

Pro-market exemption would exclude certain transactions by professional traders from specifed requirements of the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations, including trading rules, listing of transactions, reporting requirements, registration requirements and risk disclosure.

U.S. futures exchange officials said Born was off the mark. Chicago exchange officials said it it would be self-defeating for them to discard all the safeguards that have attracted customers to their markets.
"I was a little surprised she went after the FIA," Jack Sandner, chairman of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, told Reuters.
Sandner said the futures industry was only seeking a "level playing field."
Chicago Board of Trade president Tom Donovan reiterated the CBOT's support for legislation to reform the CEA.
"This legislation will give us the flexibility to address the competition" from over-the-counter markets, he said.
